notes: Summary: HarborBridge runs a low-latency chat assistant for dispatch + a reranking pipeline for manifests. Very sensitive to tail latency during peak routing windows.
Primary ask: clear SLOs (p50/p95/p99) that align between client-side UX metrics and server-side instrumentation. Need agreement before procurement.
Latency targets discussed: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for non-streaming single-response workloads (95th-case for 8k tokens).
Streaming use-case: initial token emission target p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms; but customer insists p99 semantics must reflect first-byte vs last-byte.
- Redwood server metrics: request_received -> model_infer_start -> first_token_sent -> last_token_sent -> response_sent. Server-side p95 currently measured at last_token_sent.
- Client-side metrics: connect+TLS handshake + request send + time to first meaningful token (TTFM) + time to full response. Customer sees higher tail due to network and chunked streaming behavior.
- Action item: define two SLOs per route: SLO-A (client-facing TTFM p95) and SLO-B (server inference tail p99). Link both in Console for routing/fallback logic.

Comments from CTO (paraphrased): 'We care about what the operator sees — p99 spikes during OS GC and network blips are unacceptable. Need deterministic fallback to smaller model when p95 > threshold.'
POC observations (early): token-level batching reduces cost but increases p99 under bursty micro-bursts; need dynamic batching policy with max-latency cap and preemptive flush.
SE notes: recommend Dedicated pool with 3 reserved GPUs, autoscale buffer + burst capacity for daily peak (predictable throughput ~ 600 req/s non-streaming).

SLO negotiation suggestions: set contractual p95 obligations for request-to-first-byte for streaming routes and request-to-last-byte for non-streaming, with credits tied to rolling 30-day window rather than isolated incidents.
Measurement instrumentation: agree to ship client SDK timing hooks (start_send, first_byte, last_byte) and correlate with server traces (trace_id) during POC.
Security: requires KMS integration and audit logs for every inference; Redwood to provide retention policy options (30/90/365 days) — HarborBridge prefers 90-day.
Financial: prefer 12-month committed Dedicated contract; asking for SLA language around latency credits and on-call escalation path.
Practical blocker: legal requests that p99 be defined excluding scheduled maintenance and upstream model fallback periods — need legal/SLA template.
Links: Fireflies recording, slack snippets, and transcript attached in drive (see linked_drive_docs).
Quote from product lead: 'If the p99 we commit to is measured differently than our customer-facing metric, the UI churn will kill adoption.'
key_requirements_summary: Workloads: mixed — high-throughput reranking batch jobs (non-streaming) + interactive agent chat (streaming).
Throughput target: steady 400–600 req/s non-streaming, burst to 1.5k req/s for short windows
Latency target (streaming): first-token p50 < 25–35ms, first-token p95 < 100–150ms, p99 TBD (customer wants explicit first-byte vs final-byte definitions)
Model preferences: open Llama-3-v2 / internally fine-tuned MPT variant; willing to accept quantized variants for cost if quality validated
Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model when p95 > threshold for 60s; prefer region-aware routing for NA/EU
Observability: need token-level traces, per-request cost breakdown, rolling SLO dashboard, alerting to PagerDuty for SLO breaches
commercial_notes: Preferred term: 12 months committed Dedicated + 10% burst capacity option; want price lock for model family changes.
Requested SLA clause: latency credits calculated on rolling 30-day aggregates; exclude scheduled maintenance and force-majeure.
Procurement timeline: legal + security by 2026-04, exec sign-off by 2026-05
final_recommendation: Short-term: continue POC focusing on measurement parity. Ship client SDK timing hooks and server-side trace correlation within 2 weeks.
Mid-term: proposal for 3-node Dedicated pool with autoscale buffer and quantization experiment for reranking to reduce cost per req.
SLA negotiation points to raise: explicit streaming p99 definition (first-byte vs last-byte), rolling-window crediting, and exclusion conditions for maintenance.
Win criteria for Redwood: agreed SLO spec (client+server) and successful 14-day POC where p95 targets met for 10/14 days with documented fallback behavior.
